entities.name: Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib (c. 566–c. 640) was a first cousin of the Prophet Muhammad and a Companion (ṣaḥābī) of the early Islamic community. A member of the Banu Hashim within Quraysh, he belonged to the same clan network that framed Muhammad’s kinship politics in Mecca and Medina. Traditional Islamic biographical literature (sīra and ṭabaqāt) records him among the family members who navigated the transition from Meccan aristocracy to the new Muslim polity.

Though not among the most prominent commanders or caliphs, Rabīʿah represents the Hashimite cousinage that gave the Prophet both support and internal complexity—kin who could convert, mediate, or compete as Islam reshaped Arabian social bonds. His lifespan bridges the late jāhiliyya, the Prophetic mission, and the early conquest-era caliphate, making him a useful prosopographical marker for Hashimite participation in Islam’s foundational generation.
